root_idea.summary: The root centers on security and freedom from fear, trustworthiness, and believing or affirming something as true.
root_idea.development: The two closely related orientations are inward calm and safety on one side, and trust or confirmation on the other. From these develop meanings of being secure, granting or seeking protection, entrusting, faith, trustworthy character, and entrusted property or charge.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran occurrence is the passive Form VIII perfect, normalized as a passive citation form.
Feminine active-participle inflection is presented under the common citation form آمن.
Plural active-participle inflection is presented under the singular citation form آمن.
The plural is presented under the singular nominal citation form أمانة.
This is the distinct noun أَمَنَةٌ, meaning a state or instance of security.
Feminine plural active-participle inflection is presented under the singular citation form مؤمن.
Feminine active-participle inflection is presented under the common citation form مؤمن.

senses.definition: To be, become, or feel secure and free from fear.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person or community, and with مِنْ for being secure from or free from fear of something. The Quran also uses it in rhetorical questions about assuming oneself safe from impending harm.

senses.definition: To trust or entrust someone with a person, matter, or charge.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive construction meaning to trust someone, give him charge over something, or confide a responsibility to him; it is distinct from the intransitive sense of feeling safe.

senses.definition: To render secure, protect, or grant security and safe-conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative construction: someone is made safe from a threat or granted protection, security, indemnity, or quarter.

senses.definition: To believe, affirm as true, or have faith in God, revelation, messengers, or a professed truth.
senses.usage_conditions: The verb may be used transitively, with بِ, or with لِ; believing may involve inward assent and, in some Quranic contexts, is contrasted with merely acknowledging something verbally. The construction can also express giving credit to someone.

senses.definition: To be entrusted with a person, property, or charge; to be trusted with something.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran occurrence is passive: the subject is the person to whom a trust or responsibility is entrusted.

senses.definition: Secure, safe, and free from fear.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle used adjectivally or substantivally of a person, community, town, or other setting characterized by security.

senses.definition: Faith or belief: firm assent to God, His word, and His messengers, with the corresponding confession and conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun can denote a person's faith or belief, the religious commitment associated with it, and the faith recognized as a basis of religious belonging. The lexical discussion also uses it for trustful confirmation.

senses.definition: Prayer or an act of worship, in a Quranic expression referring to an earlier prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: This specialized interpretation applies to the expression in which a previous form of worship is called īmān; it is not a general replacement for the meaning faith.

senses.definition: The revealed religious law or dispensation accepted as faith.
senses.usage_conditions: A contextual extension in which īmān denotes the prophetic religious order or the state of belonging to it.

senses.definition: A trust, entrusted property, responsibility, or charge committed to someone's care.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for concrete trusts and for a weighty responsibility or obligation entrusted to a person; the plural refers to trusts collectively.

senses.definition: A state or instance of security and relief from fear.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun for security experienced or bestowed, including the calm and repose associated with safety.

senses.definition: Trustworthy, faithful, or entrusted with a charge.
senses.usage_conditions: An adjective for a person or agent in whom trust is placed, including a guardian, depositary, or reliable bearer of a message or responsibility.
A Quranic adjectival use describing a secure setting or condition; this is distinct from the relational meaning trustworthy.

senses.definition: Security, safety, and freedom from fear; protection or an assured state of safety.
senses.usage_conditions: It may describe a condition of security, a protected state, or a place in which one is safe. The Quranic noun contrasts with fear and may carry the practical sense of protection or safe-conduct.

senses.definition: A place of safety or security.
senses.usage_conditions: A locative noun for the place or destination in which a person is safe.

senses.definition: Trusted, or regarded as safe and secure to rely upon.
senses.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective describing someone or something from which security is felt or in which trust can be placed.

senses.definition: A believer: one who affirms the truth and has faith.
senses.usage_conditions: Used substantivally or adjectivally for believing persons, with masculine and feminine forms and singular and plural inflections represented under this citation form.

senses.definition: The one who grants security and protects from fear or wrong.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic divine epithet, describing the giver of security and the one who fulfills or guarantees protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be trusted in, trustworthy, trusty, or faithful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form I stative use describing a person who is relied upon or confided in.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To say آمين after a prayer or supplication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II ritual use, especially after recitation or prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trust, confide in, or place confidence in someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader or figurative Form IV use with بِ, without the direct causative sense of granting safety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To submit to God, accept the religious law, or manifest humility and acceptance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized theological and religious use distinguished from merely professing belief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for protection, or to enter under another's protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X constructions concern seeking or accepting safe-conduct and protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Religious integrity or a sound natural disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A restricted idiomatic use in expressions praising someone's religion or innate character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person seeking protection or security for himself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare nominal use referring to one who asks or seeks protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who trusts everyone or believes whatever is heard; also one whom people trust and whose harmfulness they do not fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This expression preserves two opposing relational orientations: indiscriminate trust and being trusted by others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong, reliable she-camel not feared to stumble, tire, or become weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic animal-related adjective, understood as a passive-like form meaning secure from the stated defects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who trusts or confides in another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare contrasting use of أمين, distinct from the more usual meaning one who is trusted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An aid, assistant, or guard relied upon for strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended lexical use based on confidence in the person's ability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong or dependable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, partly figurative extension associated with freedom from fear of weakness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trustworthiness, faithfulness, fidelity, or reliable conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes a quality of character rather than the concrete trust or responsibility entrusted to someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's family or household regarded as a trust placed in his care.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized extension of the sense of something committed to one's responsibility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The choice or most highly valued part of one's property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of property regarded as secure from being exchanged or sacrificed; it is not the ordinary adjectival sense safe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Steadfast in forbearance or clemency, with no fear of losing self-restraint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use applied to a person's temper or self-control.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The prayer formula “Amen,” meaning “so be it” or “O Lord, answer.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An indeclinable expression used immediately after prayer or supplication; it is lexically distinct from the active participle أمين.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Faithful, trusting, or confiding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical adjectival use of the Form IV active participle beyond the Quranic substantive sense believer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman sought after and retained because of valuable qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare feminine derivative describing desirability and dependable worth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular kind of food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized food name associated historically with al-Maʾmūn rather than a productive semantic use of the root.

cautions: آمَنَ as a Form IV verb and آمِن as the Form I active participle are distinct lexical forms despite their similar appearance; the former primarily concerns believing or granting security, while the latter means secure or safe.
The Form VIII Quran occurrence is passive and is therefore displayed under the normalized passive perfect citation form ائْتُمِنَ.
Some classical entries contain rare, contrasting, figurative, or attributed extensions; these are kept separate from the ordinary Quranic senses rather than generalized across all contexts.

Lane's printed Quran references use historical citation conventions; no such bracketed reference has been converted into a modern verse location unless the QAC packet independently supplied that location.
